name: nextjs-webpack-callback-isclient-undefined
hook: Next.js 15.5.9 webpack callback only passes isServer, not isClient
body: The second argument to the next.config.js webpack function receives { dir, dev, isServer, buildId, config, defaultLoaders, totalPages, webpack, nextRuntime } — isClient is NOT included. Destructuring { isClient } gives undefined, and !undefined === true, so any !isClient conditional runs for ALL builds (client, server, edge). Use webpackConfig.name === 'client' or webpackConfig.name === 'server' to identify the build target.
why: Task 2476 changed webpack: (webpackConfig) to webpack: (webpackConfig, { isClient }) intending to differentiate client from server builds, but isClient is not a valid parameter in Next.js 15.5.9. This caused undici/@napi-rs/canvas to be added to externals for client builds too, breaking the browser build with _webpack.WebpackError is not a constructor during minification.

name: webpack-config-require-in-callback
hook: require works inside webpack config callbacks even when next.config.js is ESM
body: Webpack config callbacks (the function passed to webpack:) run in Node.js at build time, not at config-file-load time. This means `require` is available inside the callback even when next.config.js uses ESM imports at the top level. This allows accessing Next.js's bundled webpack modules via `require('next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack.js')` from inside the callback.
why: Next.js 15's next.config.js is ESM at the top level, but webpack bundling happens at runtime in Node.js. The callback is evaluated by Node.js directly, not by an ESM module loader. This is the bridge between the ESM config file and CommonJS webpack internals.

name: nodeprotocol-webpack-plugin-alternative-fails
hook: NodeSchemePlugin using resolverFactory.hooks.resolve causes tap undefined error in Next.js 15.5.9
body: Trying to handle node: protocol imports via a custom webpack plugin that taps resolverFactory.hooks.resolve fails with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading tap)'. In Next.js 15.5.9, resolverFactory.hooks.resolve does not exist — the approach of tapping resolveForScheme.for('node') via a plugin fails because the underlying resolver hook structure is different from expected.
why: The NodeSchemePlugin approach was technically sound in concept but failed because resolverFactory.hooks.resolve is undefined in Next.js 15.5.9s bundled webpack. The actual fix is to NOT handle node: imports at all — since undici and @napi-rs/canvas are in serverExternalPackages, webpack never processes their node: imports in browser builds.

name: resolve-alias-cannot-intercept-node-protocol
hook: resolve.alias cannot intercept node: URL scheme imports
body: webpack resolve.alias uses exact string matching (or $ suffix for exact match), but it does NOT interpret regex patterns. A key like '^node:' or '\.node$' in resolve.alias will match literal module names, not node: URL scheme imports. The '\.node$' pattern only matches file paths ending in .node, not the node: protocol.
why: The `node:` protocol is a separate resolution path in webpack 5 from module name resolution. resolve.alias operates on module names, not URL schemes.

name: serverexternalpackages-sufficient-for-node-imports
hook: packages in serverExternalPackages never have their node: imports processed by webpack browser build
body: When a package is listed in serverExternalPackages, webpack treats it as external and never analyzes its internal modules for browser builds. This means undici's internal node: imports are never encountered in the browser bundle, making any explicit node: protocol handling unnecessary.
why: The dev branch builds without any node: protocol handling because undici is already in serverExternalPackages. The previous attempts to handle node: imports were solving a problem that doesn't exist when the root cause (webpack analyzing undici internals) is prevented by serverExternalPackages.

name: node-alias-survived-after-nodeprotocol-plugin-removal
hook: The \.node$ alias and resolve.fallback.node must be kept separate from NodeSchemePlugin removal
body: When removing NodeSchemePlugin, the \.node$ resolve.alias and resolve.fallback.node: false must be kept — they are independent of the plugin. The plugin was for node: scheme handling; the alias is for .node file paths. Both are needed for the browser build to succeed. Use webpackConfig.name === 'client' as the condition for client-only webpack config changes.
why: The previous fix removed the entire block including the .node$ alias, not understanding that the alias and the plugin serve different purposes.

name: resolve-fallback-vs-resolve-alias-for-node-url-scheme
hook: resolve.fallback.node: false does NOT intercept node: URL scheme imports
body: webpack resolve.fallback.node handles 'node' bare module requests (require('node')), NOT 'node:console' URL scheme requests. The node: URL scheme is resolved via a separate webpack mechanism (resolveForScheme). To intercept node: URL scheme imports, you must use resolve.alias entries for each specific module ('node:console', 'node:crypto', etc.) or mark the package as external.
why: The previous fix added resolve.fallback.node: false thinking it would handle all node: imports, but it only handles the bare 'node' module name. The node: URL scheme is a separate resolution path in webpack 5.
